newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman to visit Montana on buffalo issue.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman to visit Montana on buffalo issue.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman Wednesday said he will visit Montana this weekend to a get a "first-hand look" at the buffalo situation in Yellowstone National Park.
"This will be a fact-finding trip. I am coming to learn and intend to sit down with as many people, with as many points of view, as possible," the secretary said in a statement.

About half of Yellowstone's historic herd has perished this winter. Hundreds have died of starvation or cold, and 1,059 have been shot or sent to slaughter as they wandered in search of food out of the park and onto Montana land.

Ranchers fear the buffalo -- also known as bison -- could spread the disease brucellosis to cattle. USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service for years has threatened to revoke the state's brucellosis-free status for cattle if they share grazing grounds with buffalo.
The inspection service backed off that policy this winter, but federal officials say Montana has continued to destroy buffalo that leave the park.
Earlier this week, Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt asked the state to stop shooting stray buffalo while a study is done on whether they pose a disease threat to cattle.
Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he will tour the buffalo capture facility in Yellowstone and participate in a town hall meeting in Gardiner, Montana.
Glickman will also meet with Montana Governor Marc Racicot and Senators Max Baucus and Conrad Burns during his one day visit to the state on Sunday, March 23.
